classification.difficultyReason: Interpret the route as two equal tangents and a major arc, derive tangent lengths and the excluded central angle, then add the straight and curved distances.

content.prompt: Point $A$ is 1 kilometre from the edge of a circular lake of radius 1 kilometre. James runs a lap around the lake starting from point $A$, as indicated below. Find the length of his journey.

spec.description: External point A, two tangent journey segments and the major journey arc. Dashed centre line carries two consecutive labels 1; dashed radii meet the tangents at marked right angles. The source's decorative lake fill is omitted.
spec.mathematics: The lake radius is 1 km and the distance from its centre to A is 2 km. Tangency points are at central angles 30 and 150 degrees; the journey follows the remaining 240-degree arc.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied lengths and geometry are visible; no calculated lengths or angles are printed.

inlines.text: Add the two tangent lengths to the length of the major arc.

answer.worked:
Let $O$ be the lake's centre and $T,U$ the tangent contact points. A radius is perpendicular to a tangent at its point of contact, and the two tangents from $A$ have equal lengths.

$$\begin{align*}
AO&=1+1=2\\
AT&=\sqrt{2^2-1^2}\\
AT&=\sqrt{3}\\
\cos\angle TOA&=\frac{1}{2}\\
\angle TOA&=\frac{\pi}{3}\\
\angle TOU\text{ (minor)}&=2\times\frac{\pi}{3}=\frac{2\pi}{3}\\
\theta\text{ (major)}&=2\pi-\frac{2\pi}{3}=\frac{4\pi}{3}\\
L&=r\theta=1\times\frac{4\pi}{3}=\frac{4\pi}{3}\\
\text{Journey length}&=2\sqrt{3}+\frac{4\pi}{3}\text{ km}
\end{align*}$$
